articleTitle: Project management techniques and the relevance of tools
publicationTitle: 1993 IEE Colloquium on Project Management Tools (Digest No: 1993/046)
abstract: Project Management can be split into two main categories: technical management-the physical integrity; and programme management-organisation, techniques, and tools. The project organisation needs to understand the techniques that can be used to control project work and the tools that are available to support those techniques. The techniques are: scope definition and structuring; time planning; budgetary planning; physical progress measurement; performance measurement; and trend analysis and forecasting. To use these techniques certain approaches must be taken and a number of philosophical tools employed in order to achieve suitable control criteria. The author gives a breakdown of these tools and how they should be used.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

abstract: The author summarises the state of software for project management and then discusses future developments in the following areas: user interfaces; the end of PERT; the multiproject environment; and schedules and CAD.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: 1993 IEE Colloquium on Project Management Tools (Digest No: 1993/046)
abstract: The technical issues of which project management tool to use are insignificant compared with the business issues-'how do I manage my people projects and priorities; what style of projects do we run; how mature is my organisation (is every project really different from all the others); and can we demonstrate we know what we are doing, and getting better at it'. The author discusses the different needs of project managers, department managers, team leaders and team members and the key project management issues they face.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: People and project management-making it happen
publicationTitle: 1993 IEE Colloquium on Project Management Tools (Digest No: 1993/046)
abstract: Corporate organisations are undergoing transition to flexible and responsive networks embracing both customers and suppliers. But the desire for change is not always matched by an awareness of how to bring it about. The author draws upon the latest batch of an ongoing series of surveys of larger organisations. They highlight the need for clear vision and sustained top management commitment. Transformation is taking longer to achieve than was first thought. In a growing number of organisations, there is disillusion, and a gulf between expectation and achievement. In particular, many managers are not being equipped with the project management and other skills to bring about corporate transformation. The author identifies the skills that are sought and suggests that new attitudes and approaches are needed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
